title: Enosh
summary: Enosh, son of seth, in the line of Seth (Genesis 5).

sorting_basis.note: Tier 4: Ussher, Annals: 235 AM, 3769 BC (no higher-tier year available).

birth.citation: Jones, Chronology of the Old Testament (15th ed., 2002), "Chronological Compendium", p. 1
birth.note: Jones prints only the AM figure here; no BC year is printed for this birth, so year_bc_ad is left null (not inferred).

birth.citation: Gen 5 cumulative begetting ages (father seth begat at 105, Gen 5:6)
Ussher, Annals of the World, First Age, §14 (paragraph numbering of the modern transcription)
Jordan, "The Chronology of the Pentateuch (Part 2)," Biblical Chronology 6:4 (April 1994), §4 "The Chronology of Genesis 4 & 5" (year list)

birth.date: 235 AM (birth year printed at the start of the enosh bar)
birth.citation: Anno Mundi Chronology Studies (unnamed compiler; a compilation of James B. Jordan's system), p. 1, chart "A.M. Chronology (Anno Mundi “Year of the World”) Genesis 5, 11:10"
birth.note: Agrees with Jordan's own published AM 235.

birth.citation: Raleigh, The History of the World (1617, EEBO-TCP A10357), Chronological Table, sig. 781b
birth.note: Year cell "918 236". To the Reader (sig. 780b): the Julian Period exceeds the yeere of the World by 682. The 905 at the end of the name is the lifespan he prints. His table also prints the death at World 1140. 236 + 905 is not 1140. Both figures are left as printed.

death.citation: Griffith & White, "Chronological Framework of Ancient History. 4: Dating Creation and the Deluge," ARJ 16 (2023): 475–489, section "AP-31: Death of Huang Di/Enosh: 2865/2864 B.C."
death.note: CFAH identifies the Chinese patriarch Huang Di with Enosh; Hebrew-number path gives 2864 B.C., Chinese paths 2865 and 2864 B.C.
Not stated in the Jones sources read (Chart No. 1; Chronology of the Old Testament 15th ed. 2002, Chronological Compendium p. 1). Leave empty until verified.

death.citation: Ussher, Annals of the World, First Age, §25 (paragraph numbering of the modern transcription)
Jordan, "The Chronology of the Pentateuch (Part 2)," Biblical Chronology 6:4 (April 1994), §4 "The Chronology of Genesis 4 & 5" (year list)
Anno Mundi Chronology Studies (unnamed compiler; a compilation of James B. Jordan's system), p. 1, chart "A.M. Chronology (Anno Mundi “Year of the World”) Genesis 5, 11:10"
death.note: Slip in the compilation: 235 + 905 = 1140 (Gen 5:11), as Jordan and the Masoretic arithmetic have; the chart prints 1130. Differs from Jordan's own published figure(s): AM 1140.

death.citation: Raleigh, The History of the World (1617, EEBO-TCP A10357), Chronological Table, sig. 782a
death.note: Year cell "1822 1140". To the Reader (sig. 780b): the Julian Period exceeds the yeere of the World by 682.
